During fine-tuning the model maximises a **combined objective**: the supervised task loss plus the language-modelling loss as an auxiliary term, **with the auxiliary weight λ set to 0.5**.

**The objective (page 3)**

L₃(C) = L₂(C) + λ · L₁(C)  (Eq. 5)

- **L₂(C)** is the supervised objective, Σ₍ₓ,ᵧ₎ log P(y | x₁,…,xₘ) (Eq. 4). Here P(y | x₁,…,xₘ) = softmax(hₗᵐ W_y), where hₗᵐ is the final transformer block's activation, fed into an added linear output layer W_y (Eq. 3) (page 3).
- **L₁(C)** is the standard language-modelling objective, Σᵢ log P(uᵢ | uᵢ₋ₖ,…,uᵢ₋₁; Θ) (Eq. 1), applied to the labelled dataset C (page 3).

**The weight (page 5)**

In the fine-tuning details, the paper states "λ was set to 0.5."

**Why the auxiliary term is included**

- The authors found it helped learning by "(a) improving generalization of the supervised model, and (b) accelerating convergence," which matches prior work (page 3).
- In the ablation study, it helped on the NLI tasks and QQP. Larger datasets tended to benefit from it, but smaller datasets did not (page 8).
